title: Chapter 3 Quiz 9
description: Comparing one value with several constants.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: When is a **Case** structure useful?
options: When one data item is compared with several constant values
questions.explanation: The data is successively compared to constant values.

questions.question: In a Case structure, what does the **Default / Other** part do?
options: It runs when no value matches
questions.explanation: Default actions run when none of the listed values matches. This part may be missing.

questions.question: Several values can be grouped on the same line if their actions are identical.
questions.explanation: The course notes this: values with identical actions can be grouped.

questions.question: Complete the algorithm that displays the nature of a character.
questions.code:
Declare c As Character
Input(c)
{{1}} c Of
    'A'..'Z': Display('Uppercase letter')
    'a'..'z': Display('Lowercase letter')
    '0'..'9': Display('Digit')
    {{2}}: Display('Neither letter nor digit')
EndCase
questions.explanation: Case introduces the structure. Default handles every other character.

questions.question: Run the character algorithm for each input.
questions.explanation: Ranges 'A'..'Z', 'a'..'z' and '0'..'9' select the first three; everything else is Default.

questions.question: Which structure is better to test whether a menu choice is 1, 2, 3 or 4?
questions.explanation: One value compared to several constants is the job of Case.

questions.question: Put the lines of this Case algorithm in order.
questions.explanation: Declare, read, open Case, list the values, close Case.
